NDT training in Newport News: how it works for Newport News employers and technicians

Short answer: NDT training for Newport News employers and technicians is delivered live online or onsite at your own shop, yard or facility on the Peninsula. Atlantis NDT has no classroom in Newport News. An ASNT NDT Level III teaches Level I, II and III courses in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET based on ASNT SNT-TC-1A, and supports employer examinations and certification. Cohort and onsite quotes are returned within one business day.

Newport News is not a typical NDT market. The city is dominated by one very large shipyard building nuclear-powered aircraft carriers and submarines, and around it sits a supplier and subcontractor base that has to meet Navy requirements for inspection, documentation and personnel qualification. That shapes everything about training here: the codes, the acceptance criteria, the record-keeping and the expectation that a technician's qualification can be traced, line by line, to a written programme.

It also means you should be clear about what any outside training provider can and cannot do. The shipyard runs its own internal NDT qualification programme for its own workforce. Navy work adds NAVSEA requirements that the employer is responsible for meeting. What we provide is SNT-TC-1A-based training, examination support and Level III help for the supplier companies, fabricators, ship repair contractors, machine shops and industrial employers that make up the rest of the Peninsula's inspection market, and for individuals building the foundation that any of those employers will expect.

Request a Newport News training quote and tell us your methods, levels, head-count and which specifications your customers impose.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses available in Newport News

Each course follows the SNT-TC-1A body of knowledge for its method. For Peninsula cohorts we steer practical exercises toward what the local supplier base actually inspects: welded steel structure and piping for marine use, castings and forgings, machined non-magnetic components and heavy-section welds.

MethodLevelsWhat Newport News employers use it forPrerequisite
UTI, II, IIIWeld examination on structural and piping assemblies built for naval and commercial ships; lamination checks on plate; thickness gauging in ship repairLevel I: written-practice entry rules. Level II: Level I plus documented experience
PAUTII, IIIEncoded weld examination on heavy fabrications and piping where the customer specification allows it; corrosion mappingConventional UT Level II first
TOFDII, IIIFlaw sizing on thick-section welds in heavy fabrication and power-plant componentsUT Level II
RTI, II, IIIPipe and pressure-boundary welds, castings, film and digital interpretation for supplier quality programmesVirginia radiation-safety requirements apply to anyone handling sources
MTI, IIStructural and fatigue-sensitive welds, forgings, fittings and foundationsWritten-practice entry rules
PTI, IIStainless, copper-nickel and other non-magnetic piping and components common in shipboard systemsWritten-practice entry rules
VTI, IIWeld visual, fit-up and dimensional checks on every assembly; the first examination on almost every jobWritten-practice entry rules
ETI, II, IIIHeat-exchanger and condenser tubing in power and industrial plants; surface crack detection on aircraft and precision componentsNone; prior UT or MT experience helps

VT, MT and PT: the foundation. In a shipbuilding economy, visual, magnetic particle and penetrant examinations account for a large share of inspections, and they are where most new technicians start. Our courses go further than the basics on the things marine suppliers get audited on: surface preparation, lighting and viewing conditions, magnetising technique and field direction, penetrant process control, and precise description of indications. Shipboard piping systems use a lot of non-magnetic material, so PT gets real attention in Peninsula cohorts.

UT. UT Level I and II courses cover sound physics, calibration, straight-beam lamination and thickness work, and angle-beam weld examination, with practical exercises on plate and pipe welds similar to those a marine fabricator produces. Candidates can gauge their readiness with our UT Level 2 practice questions.

RT. Radiography remains important for pressure-boundary and piping welds and for castings. The course covers exposure technique, image quality indicators, film and digital radiography and interpretation. Radiation safety is regulated separately by Virginia (see below).

PAUT and TOFD. Advanced UT courses for experienced UT Level II technicians cover focal laws, encoded scanning, setup files, data analysis and flaw sizing. Whether they can be applied on a given job depends on the customer's specification, and in naval work that decision belongs to the prime contractor and the Navy, not to the technician.

ET. Eddy current courses cover impedance-plane interpretation, probe selection, calibration and either tubing or surface work, depending on whether a cohort supports power and industrial plants or aviation maintenance.

Level III. Live online preparation for the ASNT Basic and Method examinations plus procedure-writing practice. See ASNT Level III training.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Newport News, step by step

  1. Written practice. The employer adopts a written practice based on SNT-TC-1A that defines training, experience, examinations, vision and recertification for each method and level. Where the employer also supplies Navy work, its programme must additionally meet the requirements its customers flow down, which the employer's Level III reconciles.
  2. Formal training. Complete the classroom hours the written practice requires, online, onsite or blended. The training-requirements matrix shows SNT-TC-1A recommended figures; customer specifications can require more.
  3. Supervised experience. Log documented hours performing the method under a certified Level II or III.
  4. General examination on principles, equipment and terminology.
  5. Specific examination on the employer's procedures, equipment and acceptance standards, which for Navy suppliers usually means the criteria flowed down in the purchase order.
  6. Practical examination on real specimens, graded by a Level III or a qualified examiner working under one.
  7. Vision examination: near-vision acuity at least annually and colour-contrast differentiation per the written practice.
  8. Certification signed by the employer.
  9. Recertification at the interval the written practice sets (SNT-TC-1A recommends no more than five years), by examination or documented performance as permitted.

More on the employer's role: SNT-TC-1A training and certification.

Online, live-virtual or onsite NDT training for Newport News crews

  • Live online. Real-time instructor-led theory for Level I and II and Level III preparation, scheduled to fit shift work. Suppliers whose staff work second or third shift often prefer this. See online NDT training.
  • Onsite at your facility. An ASNT Level III-led team teaches and examines at your shop on your equipment and representative specimens, so the specific and practical examinations reflect the work you actually do. See corporate NDT training.
  • Blended. Online theory followed by an onsite practical and examination block.

Scheduling on the Peninsula follows the shipbuilding and ship repair calendar: delivery milestones for supplier assemblies, availability periods for ships in repair across Hampton Roads, and outage seasons at power plants in the region. Many suppliers also need to train new hires in batches as contracts ramp up. Tell us your milestone dates and we will plan training and examinations to land before them. Ask about onsite training for your Newport News crew.

Practical examinations are always hands-on with real equipment and specimens, never remote.

Where NDT technicians work in Newport News

Naval shipbuilding and its supply chain. Newport News Shipbuilding, part of HII, builds the Navy's nuclear-powered aircraft carriers and, with a partner yard, its nuclear submarines, and also performs carrier refueling and complex overhaul. The yard trains and qualifies its own inspectors internally, including through its long-established Apprentice School. The broader opportunity for outside training lies in the hundreds of suppliers, fabricators and subcontractors across Hampton Roads and beyond that build components and assemblies for the yard and must meet the inspection requirements flowed down to them.

The Navy specifications local employers ask about. Navy surface ship and submarine work references NAVSEA technical publications, including T9074-AS-GIB-010/271 for NDT method and personnel requirements and MIL-STD-2035 for acceptance criteria, alongside NAVSEA fabrication and welding requirements. These are named here as context for what Peninsula employers ask for. Atlantis training is SNT-TC-1A-based; meeting NAVSEA personnel-qualification requirements, and any examinations those requirements specify, is the responsibility of the employer's programme and its Level III. Nuclear propulsion work adds further controls and access requirements set by the Navy and the prime contractor.

Ship repair across the harbour. The Peninsula is part of the Hampton Roads ship repair market, where contractors perform MT, UT thickness, VT and PT on Navy and commercial vessels. Commercial work usually follows ABS or other classification society rules and U.S. Coast Guard requirements.

Aerospace, research and aviation maintenance. NASA Langley Research Center in neighbouring Hampton and the aviation units at Joint Base Langley-Eustis support aerospace research, aircraft and rotorcraft maintenance. Aerospace employers frequently require NAS 410 qualification, which is a separate scheme; some industrial and research employers work to SNT-TC-1A.

Power generation. Dominion Energy's Surry Power Station, a two-unit nuclear plant across the James River in Surry County, brings outage work where in-service inspection follows ASME Section XI. Nuclear UT typically needs performance demonstration qualification in addition to SNT-TC-1A training, and utilities impose their own access programmes.

Bridges, tunnels and terminals. The James River Bridge, the Monitor-Merrimac Memorial Bridge-Tunnel and the port and energy terminals on the Peninsula need steel and structural inspection, typically to AWS D1.5 for bridge welding and owner specifications for everything else.

Radiography licensing in Virginia. Virginia became an NRC Agreement State on March 31, 2009. The Virginia Department of Health's Office of Radiological Health licenses radioactive material, including industrial radiography sources, under the Virginia Radiation Protection Regulations (12VAC5-481), with regulatory guidance for industrial radiography programmes. Radiographer training and certification follow those regulations and the company's licence conditions. That is separate from SNT-TC-1A RT certification: most Peninsula radiographers need both, one covering radiation safety and the other technique and interpretation. Out-of-state crews working in Virginia need to follow the state's reciprocity process.

What employers ask for. A current method certification and the written practice behind it, complete training and experience records, a current vision record, and for defence work the security and access vetting the prime contractor requires. Many shipyard-area jobs also ask for a TWIC card. For earnings information, see our NDT salary guide, which cites public sources.

Level III services and written practices for Newport News NDT companies

Supplier audits in a naval shipbuilding supply chain are thorough. An auditor will read the written practice, check that it covers every method and technique in use, trace a sample of technicians through training, experience, examination and vision records, and compare procedures against the specifications on the purchase order. Smaller suppliers often find their written practice was adapted from a template years ago and no longer matches what they do.

  • Written practice development and review to align your document with your actual methods and customer requirements. See written practice development.
  • Examination preparation and grading under ASNT Level III oversight, including specific examinations built around the acceptance criteria your customers impose.
  • Procedure writing and review, with a Level III reviewing technique details and record formats.
  • Audit readiness: a structured review of certification files before a customer or registrar audit.

See our SNT-TC-1A guidance for background. Book a Level III consultation ahead of your next supplier audit.

Practise before the practical exam

Our Practical NDT 3D simulator covers 12 NDT methods across 5 environments: an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. Peninsula fabrication trainees usually get the most from the welding workshop, and aviation maintenance trainees from the hangar. It is a rehearsal tool for setups, coverage and interpretation between classes. It does not replace hands-on training, logged experience or the practical examination on real specimens.

Your instructor

Training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. He sets course content, oversees examinations and reviews written practices and procedures for employer clients.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Newport News

How do I get NDT certified in Newport News?

Join or be sponsored by an employer with an SNT-TC-1A written practice, complete the training hours, log supervised experience, pass the general, specific and practical examinations and a vision test, and your employer certifies you. We provide training, exam preparation and Level III support online or at the employer's site.

Can I take NDT training online in Virginia?

Yes, for theory. Live online classes cover the classroom portion of Level I and II and Level III preparation. Practical training and examinations are hands-on.

Can your training get me qualified to work inside the shipyard?

No outside course does that on its own. The shipyard qualifies its own workforce under its internal programme. Solid SNT-TC-1A training in VT, MT, PT and UT is useful background, and many supplier and ship repair employers in the area certify under SNT-TC-1A-based programmes.

How long does UT Level 2 training take?

Your employer's written practice sets it. SNT-TC-1A recommends minimum training and experience hours; experience usually takes longest. See the training-requirements matrix.

Do I need a license for radiography in Virginia?

The company needs a Virginia radioactive materials licence or machine registration, and radiographers must meet the training and certification requirements in Virginia's regulations and the licence. That is separate from SNT-TC-1A RT certification.

What does NDT training cost in Newport News?

We do not publish prices. It depends on method, level, group size, delivery mode and any Level III support. Send the details and we quote within one business day.

Is ASNT certification recognised by Newport News employers?

SNT-TC-1A-based programmes are widely used by industrial, repair and supplier employers in the region. Navy work adds NAVSEA requirements that the employer's programme must also meet, and aerospace employers may require NAS 410. Recognition runs through the employer's written practice.

What is NAVSEA Tech Pub 271, and do you train to it?

It is the NAVSEA publication covering NDT methods and personnel requirements for Navy work. We mention it because local employers ask about it, but our training is SNT-TC-1A-based. Meeting Tech Pub 271 requirements is handled by the employer's programme.

Which method should I start with?

VT and MT, then PT. They are the most widely used methods in shipbuilding and ship repair. Add UT once you have experience.

Can you train a batch of new hires at our shop?

Yes. We run onsite cohorts and examinations under your written practice, timed to your contract ramp-up.

Does my certification transfer to a new employer?

Not automatically. The new employer reviews your records and certifies you under its own written practice.

Do you offer Level III preparation?

Yes, live online. See Level III training and our full training catalogue.
